notes: Confirmed. The body reads selector 0x53. Values 5..35 return value-5; values below 5 or above 35 take the fallback and return 30. Thus the output is bounded to 0..30. Its caller stores the returned value as a byte-sized value, consistent with the normalization name.

The body calls f_7001812610(0xffff,0xffff), returns false if that result is below 8, then queries selector 0x14. It returns 1 only when the low byte is below 6: after subtraction by 6, CC_CS is true for unsigned >=6 and selects 0. The proposed name incorrectly said status >=6; the corrected name matches the actual predicate. Callers branch on the result as a Boolean.

Confirmed. The body loads the pointer at input+0 and returns immediately if null. Otherwise it masks x2 and x3 to one bit and tail-calls the accepted load_bink_movie_file helper. Callers inspect the returned low bit as a Boolean/status value.

Confirmed. The body clears the byte through global pointer 0x7002280d58 and 64 bytes through 0x7002280d50, calls the accepted parse_equipment_descriptions helper, then tail-calls f_7000412800. The accepted callee’s body resolves EquipmentDescription.xml and frontend//rtts//EquipmentDescriptions.xml; callers include RTTI subsystem initialization. The proposed setup/parse name is supported.

Confirmed. The body loads the pointer at input+0. For a nonnull pointer it calls the accepted attribute_record_pointer_get_or_default helper; for null it calls the default singleton getter and then the same helper. Both paths tail-call the common forwarding helper. Direct callers use the result in attribute-record flows.
